POSTURE & POSTURAL DEFECTS: WEEK 1 TABLE TENNIS Objectives: At the end of the lesson, learners should be able to: 1. Narrate the history and development of table tennis 2. Highlight the Nature of the game of Table Tennis 3. State the facilities and equipment in Table Tennis 4. Explain the basic skills and techniques of the game HISTORY OF TABLE TENNIS. Nobody is sure of the origin of Table Tennis but there is the general belief that it started in England in about 1890 and was then regarded as PARLOUR GAME because it was primarily an indoor game. It was called different names such as “Ping Pong” “Indoor tennis” and “Gossima”. In 1922, the rules were established under the English initiative. The name Table Tennis was given by the Parker brothers. The International Table Tennis was formed in 1926 with its headquarters in Berlin. The beginning of table tennis in Nigeria is not very clear but the coming of the white men especially the missionaries who introduced schools also brought the game. In 1951 the Nigeria Table Tennis Federation (NTTF) was formed. Since then, there has been a lot of competitions at local, states, federal and international levels. TABLE TENNIS

NATURE OF THE GAME 1. It is a recreational sport. 2. It is a point scoring game. 3. It is played by boys and girls, men and women. 4. Celluloid egg is used in playing the game. 5. It is best played as indoor game. 6. The game of table tennis is played on table 7. It is played by two or four players i.e. singles, doubles and mixed doubles.

CONCEPT OF TABLE TENNIS The game begins with a serve from the server after a toss for choice of service. The ball must hit the server’s table before crossing the net into the opponent’s court. A point is awarded to a player who wins the rally. Players change service after every two points have been scored. A player winning 11points wins the game. In case of a tie at 10points, a player must win two more points to win the game. Matches are played to the best of 3 or 5 games. EVALUATION QUESTIONS a. WEEK 2 TABLE TENNIS Objectives: At the end of the lesson, learners should be able to: 1. Itemize the rules and regulation in Table tennis 2. State the officials in Table Tennis and their duties 3. Mention the similarities between Table Tennis and Tennis game Similarities between Table Tennis and Tennis game 1. They are all striking games. 2. They are played with racket. 3. The service is decided by a toss. 4. Both have same types of play, i.e. singles, doubles and mixed doubles. 5. Either player can score a point irrespective of who is serving. 6. Both games involve a rally. 7. They have similar skills such as forehand stroke, backhand stroke and smashing. RULES IN TABLE TENNIS 1) A served ball touching the net and falling on the opponent’s court is a ‘LET’. 2) The ball must bounce on the opponent’s court before it is played. 3) A striker should not touch the table, the net or its support during play. 4) There is change of service after every five points. 5) It is a fault to spin the ball upwards before hitting it during service. 6) The ball must be shown before the service is made. 7) It is a LET if the ball breaks while in play. 8) No part of the body is allowed to touch the table during play. 9) It is a LET, if the receiver is not ready. 10) A player scores one point each time an opponent makes an error, when he/she is serving or receiving. WEEK 3 HANDBALL Objectives: At the end of the lesson, learners should be able to: 1. Narrate the history and development of Handball

2. Highlight the Nature of the game of Handball 3. State the facilities and equipment in Handball 4. Explain the basic skills and techniques of the game HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT OF HANDBALL Handball game was introduced in Germany by a gymnastic master called Korad Koch. The Greeks and Romans called the game “CATCHBALL”, but in1919 Carl Schelenz was the first to call the game HANDBALL and also designed uniform rules for the game. He as a physical Education teacher in Berlin, England where he reduces the size of the field that was so large to 40m by 20m and this earned him the name “FATHER OF HANDBALL” since the dimension has been adopted as an international size. NATURE OF THE GAME 1. The game can be played by all ages. 2. It is both indoor and outdoor game. 3. It is a goal scoring game. 4. It is a team game. 5. It can be played on a Hard court or Green grass. 6. Its skills are natural which makes the game simple. 7. Its rules are not many compared with other ball games. 8. It is played by two teams of 7 players (6 court players and 1 goalkeeper). 9. The game is played in two halves of 30 minutes each with a break of 10 minutes. PLAYING THE GAME The game is started at the centre with a Throw-off, while all the players remain in their own half of the court and the defender shall be at 3m away from the starting team. The player is permitted to stop, catch, throw or bounce the ball in any manner, by using the hands, arms, head, thighs, knees or any part of the body except the leg. The ball must not be held by any player for more than 3 minutes on a spot i.e. while not moving. A player may take a minimum of 3 steps while holding the ball. It is allowed to bounce the ball once or repeatedly and to catch it again with one or both hands, either while running or standing. A player is also allowed to roll the ball on the ground repeatedly with one hand either running or standing and then to catch it with one or both hands. FACILITIES IN HANDBALL GAME 1. The goal posts

2. The court – cemented floor/green grass. EQUIPMENT IN HANDBALL GAME 1. The ball. 2. The net. 3. A pair of jersey. 4. Goalkeeper’s gloves. 5. Canvas. 6. Whistle. SKILLS IN HANDBALL GAME i. Throwing and Catching.

ii. Passing. iii. Dodging. iv. Shooting. v. Fast break vi. Goal Keeping. vii. Attacking/offensive play. viii. Dribbling EVALUATION QUESTION: 1. Handball game was originated from _______________ 2. OFFICIALS IN HANDBALL 1. The Referee (Court Referee and Goal line Referee) 2. The Time keeper 3. The Scorer COURT DIMENSION Length (Side line/Touch line) 40m Breadth (Goal line) 20m Penalty Throw 7m RULES AND REGULATIONS IN HANDBALL 1. Every player shall be in his/her own half of the court at the start of the game and when a goal is scored. 2. Players can be substituted at any time of the game from the substitute’s place. 3. Any player gaining possession of the ball shall not take more than three steps before the release of the ball. 4. A goal cannot be scored direct from a THROW – OFF or Centre passes. 5. A goal may be scored direct from a free throw. 6. If the ball wholly crosses the touchline on the ground or in the air, the play shall be re- started by a throw-in. 7. Only the goal keeper is allowed to enter or to be in the goal area. 8. A player who leaves the court for ungentlemanly conduct shall be disqualified for the rest of the game. 9. A ball that returns from the goal area out into the playing area remains in play. 10. A player who is recognized as goal keeper may become a court player at any time similarly; a court player may also become a goal keeper but not during penalty throw. LANGUAGE OF HANDBALL GAME 1. Substitution. 2. Time out. 3. Free-Throw. 4. Throw-on. 5. Throw-in. 6. Corner-Throw. 7. Goal-Throw. 8. Penalty-Throw. 9. Referee’s Throw. 10. 1. For faulty substitution of goal keeper. 2. If there is a dangerous play. 3. If a court player intentionally enters his goal area for defensive purpose. 4. WEEK 5 ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION Objectives: At the end of the lesson, learners should be able to: 1. Define Environment pollution 2. State the types of pollution 3. Highlight the effects of pollution in the environment. 4. Enumerate sources of pollution 5. Mention ways through which pollution can be prevented. ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION

➢ Environmental Pollution is the release of contaminated and harmful substances and materials into the surroundings which affect living things negatively. Pollution occurs to air, water and land. ➢ It is the release of unwanted substances into the surrounding. ➢ The act of contaminating or polluting can either be intentionally or accidentally. TYPES OF POLLUTION 1. AIR POLLUTION: - This is the release of harmful and unwanted substance into the air, pollution of the atmosphere. CAUSES OF AIR POLLUTION 1. Cigarette smoking 2. Smoke from burnt tyres 3. Dust from sand 4. Smoke from vehicle exhaust pipe and generators 5. Bad odour from poorly constructed soak away 6. Odour from refuse heaps or containers 7. Smoke from factories 8. Bad odour from dead bodies and toilets 2. WATER POLLUTION: - Water pollution is the making of water impure, unfit and dirty for human consumption or use of the water bodies. CAUSES OF WATER POLLUTION 1. Dumping of waste into the rivers, streams and lakes 2. Factory waste, such as oil firms, detergents and suspended particles 3. Applying chemicals into the rivers, streams, lakes, during fishing 4. Throwing or defecation into the water

5. Infected people taking their bath in the river where people fetch water for drinking 3. LAND POLLUTION: - This is the contamination of the land which affects its productivity level negatively. CAUSES OF LAND POLLUTION 1. Use of chemicals 2. Oil spillage 3. Dumping of refuse in an unauthorized place 4. Damage to oil pipeline as a result of oil bunkering 4. NOISE POLLUTION: - This is the release of unpleasant sound in the environment, annoying and potentially harmful sound in the environmental. CAUSES OF NOISE POLLUTION 1. Sounds of drum during festivals 2. Uses of drum and loud speakers in churches, mosques and parties 3. Increasing the volume of radio and television at close range 4. Use of sirens by escort and law enforcement agencies 5. Activities of commercial music suppliers SOURCES OF POLLUTION 1) Oil spillage. 2) Gasses from vehicles and automobile engines. 3) Cigarette smoking. 4) Industrial and factory waste. 5) Bush burning. 6) Refuse and sewage disposal. 7) Erosion. 8) War disaster. 9) Noise.

EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION 1) Danger to human life and animals as it affects the growth of plants. 2) Reduce the productivity level of the soil. 3) Climatic change or change in weather condition 4) Death of plants and animals due to spread of diseases 5) Difficulty in breathing as it brings about sneezing and possibly cough 6) There will be outbreak of water-borne diseases e.g. typhoid, dysentery, guinea worms 7) There will be scarcity of land to buy and shortage of water animals e.g. fish, shrimps, crayfish etc. 8) It causes high blood pressure or hypertension 9) It causes damage to the ear drum 10) Agriculture will be difficult to practice because the land has been polluted PREVENTIVE MEASURE OF ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION 1. Ensure good health habits 2. Industries/factories should not be located near dwelling houses 3. All smoky vehicles on our roads should be banned 4. Avoid using dangerous chemicals 5. Factories should dispose their waste properly instead of using rivers, lakes and streams 6. Reduce the volume of your radio and television 7. Burst or damage pipes should be repaired 8. Provision of good public toilets 9. Burn or bury all wastes from the house 10. Water ways for erosion should be constructed EVALUATION QUESTION. 1. What is pollution? 2. WEEK 7 CONSUMER HEALTH, Objectives: At the end of the lesson, learners should be able to: 1. Define consumer health 2. State the measures to be taken before consuming canned foods 3. Highlight the important of consumer health 4. Enumerate precaution measures for consumers 5. Explain the effective use of health services. A Consumer could be defined as a person who consumes, utilizes or uses up consumable products such as foods, drugs, creams etc. It can also be defined as an individual who makes the final use of goods and services. Consumer health can be defined as all the measures that are often taken to protect the unsuspecting buyer or consumer from buying and using fake or harmful products and services. The importance of consumer health 1. It gives the consumer guidance on what to buy. 2. It provides the consumer the necessary information about the goods. 3. It promotes good health. 4. It helps the consumer to know his/her rights. 5. It helps to avoid purchasing fake drugs. 6. It provides the consumer with maximum satisfaction of his/her money. 7. It helps to promote the standard of health product e. g. drugs or foods. THE GENERAL PRECAUTIONAL MEASURES FOR CONSUMERS 1. Inspect consumable goods before purchasing or buying. 2. Do not eat foods from a rusted tin/can. 3. Look for the manufactured date. Check the expiry date. Do not buy/purchase dented or leaking canned foods. Purchase your consumable goods from registered shops, supermarkets and restaurants. Check meat, fish from the seller before buying. It must not be greenish in colour. CONSUMER’S RIGHT

1. A consumer has the right to move around and inspect what he/she want to buy. 2. The composition of the nutrient must be displayed. 3. Items bought but not satisfactory can be returned to the place of purchase, if it has not been opened or tampered with. 4. The product must carry expiry date. 5. The consumer has the right of choice of food items displayed. USES OF HEALTH SERVICES The available health services are health center, maternity homes, health units, clinics and hospitals. The health services are the medium through which health of the country is taken care of by the government. The community serves as the consumer that utilizes the health services made available by government by visiting the hospitals to receive adequate treatment. EVALUATION QUESTION. 1. Define consumer health 2. State five measures to be taken before consuming canned foods 3. Highlight five importance of consumer health ASSIGNMENT: Mention the consumer’s right. WEEK 8 POSTURE AND POSTURAL DEFECTS Objectives: At the end of the lesson, learners should be able to: 1. Define posture 2. State the factors that promote good posture 3. Highlight general causes of poor posture 4. Enumerate types of postural defects 5. Mention the general corrective measures of postural defect. Posture means the position in which the body is being carried or held up. There is a correct posture of the body for everything we do either standing, sitting, walking, running and sleeping. Good posture is an erect position whereby there is neither forward nor backward bending of the spinal column.

Factors that promote good posture 1. Balance diet. 2. Physical exercise. 3. Occupation. 4. Good body carriage. 5. Good health habit. 6. Early detection of problems and quick possible correction. GENERAL CAUSES OF POOR POSTURE 1. Injury sustained from accident. 2. Lack of regular exercise, rest and sleep. 3. Improper diet or malnutrition. 4. Too much pressure on the back particularly due to occupation or during pregnancy. 5. Prolonged sitting or standing position. 6. Excessive body weight (Obesity) and or rapid growth in children 7. Carrying of heavy load on one shoulder. 8. Wearing of high heel shoes. 9. Faulty bone formation. 10. Imitation or habit formation e.g. walking. TYPES OF POSTURAL DEFECTS 1. Kyphosis (Hunch back or rounded back). 2. Scoliosis. 3. Bowed - leg.

4. Knocked Knee 5. Flat foot. Lordosis (Hollow back). 6. Rigid spine or stiff neck. 7. Abducted scapular. GENERAL CORRECTIVE MEASURES OF POSTURAL DEFECTS AND WAYS OF MAITAINING GOOD POSTURE 1. Always maintain head up when walking. 2. Eat balanced diet. 3. Take regular exercise.

4. Sitting on standard seat e.g. for the students. 5. Have correct standing position. 6. To educate the public about the causes of these defects. 7. To maintain good writing position. A corrective Sandal

WEEK 9 (AQUATICS) SWIMMING Objectives: At the end of the lesson, learners should be able to: 1 Define aquatics 2 Narrate the history and development of aquatics 3 State the facilities and equipment in aquatics 4 Highlight the importance of aquatics Aquatics means all forms of movement activities performed on water. Examples of such activities are: swimming, diving, canoeing, boating, water polo, water skiing, kayaking etc.

Brief history of swimming Swimming has been recorded as one of the oldest forms of human physical activities. It has been a part of the culture of many civilization of the world. No one could have been said to be the first swimmer. It is believed that both human being and animals have been swimming for certain reasons which include: 1. For recreational purposes. 2. Learning swimming as a matter of need. 3. In order to save lives of the drowned souls. 4. In attempt to search for food for survival. It is also believed that early swimmers imitated animals in water which leads to the first primitive style “The dog paddle” being the actual imitation of the movement of dog in the water. The first actual record of swimming was established by studying Mosaic dug up in Pompey Rome. NATURE OF SWIMMING 1. Swimming is an individual sport. 2. Swimming is a water or aquatic activity. 3. It can be carried out in natural waters e.g. streams, rivers, lakes and modern swimming pools. 4. It is taken by boys and girls, men and women. 5. It is an Olympic sport. 6. It is a medal scoring sport. 7. It can be for either recreation / competition SWIMMING FACILITIES 1. Diving board 2. Changing room 3. Shower room 4. Toilet 5. Streams, lakes, rivers etc. 6. Swimming pool 7. Railings

SWIMMING EQUIPMENT 1. Swimming trunk/suits. 2. Floaters for beginners/learners. 3. Shoe fins for learners. 4. Goggles. 5. Head gear (women). 6. Towel. 7. Whistles for officials. 8. Rubber tubes for learners.
IMPORTANCE OF SWIMMING 1. It is a good form of exercise for all part of the body. 2. It provides recreational activities. 3. It brings about relaxation.

4. It makes every swimmer a potential life safer. 5. It saves one from drowning (for survival). 6. It helps to relieve tension, nervousness and promotes skills. 7. It helps to provide food e.g. fisherman. 8. It promotes good physical fitness and health. Evaluation Question 1. Define swimming 2. Explain briefly the history of swimming 3. Highlight the safety precautions in swimming Exercises necessary for beginners A beginner in swimming should have confidence and there are many ways of improving this, which are;

1. Water is very friendly and must not be made an enemy. 2. Any form of fear of water should be removed. 3. To enter the shallow end of the pool in a gradual manner. 4. To dip self into the water keeping eyes open and holding breath all along. 5. Each time out of water, not to use hand to brush water off the face. 6. To breath in and out deeply each time out of water. 7. To beat the water The basic swimming skills/strokes 1. Freestyle. 2. Front crawl.
3. Backstroke. 4. Breast stroke.
5. Butterfly stroke. 6. Diving.

Officials in swimming 1. The referee. 2. A starter. 3. A Chief Judge. 4. Turning Judges. 5. Chief Time Keeper. 6. Placing Judges. 7. Time keepers. 8. Announcers. 9. Stroke Judges Recorder. 10. Life Guard Safety precautions in swimming 1. Do not swim alone 2. Do not walk or run closely beside the swimming pool because it is often wet and slippery. 3. Always swim at the shallow end of the swimming pool as a beginner. 4. Do not eat or chew anything when in water. 5. Bathing caps should be worn in the pool by lady swimmers

6. Do not blow your nose, urinate or spit into the swimming pool. 7. A swimmer should take a bath before entering into the swimming pool. 8. Do not swim immediately after meal to avoid stomach cramp. 9. Learn how to float in water. 10. Do not dive headlong into the pool. 11. Do not swim when you are sick or ill. 12. Never push or throw anyone into the pool/water. 13. Never pretend to be drowning. 14. Walk into the swimming pool to ascertain the depth of the water before diving. 15. Anybody suffering from any form of skin diseases should not use the pool. Evaluation Questions: 1. Mention exercises necessary for beginners 2.
